answer: Intermittent arrival gate: each new identity enters through a scheduled quiet slot and must keep first requests inside a narrow delay band over rolling windows. Colliding bursts from many fresh identities defer into a dune of delayed admission, making shared launch spikes visible and rate-limited. The atlas of accepted arrival shapes keeps only identities that sustain spaced bursts; replayed or synchronized patterns get no quota. An attacker pays per fake identity by parking it on a forced idle ledge through the cool-down and forfeiting early request quota.
